subject: Social Studies
name: JHS 3 Social Studies
description: The JHS 3 Social Studies curriculum focuses on environmental issues, natural and human resources, family life, culture and national identity, law and order, socio-economic development, and nationhood.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate skills in dealing with environmental challenges

indicators.description: Examine air pollution as an environmental challenge

exemplars.description: Explain what air pollution means.
Identify activities in the environment that lead to air pollution, including fumes from vehicles, industry and smoke from fires.
Discuss the effects of air pollution, including causing health problems such as asthma.
Discuss ways to prevent air pollution.
Do a project in the community to educate members on the ways to reduce air pollution.

contentStandards.description: Evaluate the sources and ways of conserving energy

indicators.description: Assess global sources and the means of conserving energy

exemplars.description: Identify global energy sources and conservation in countries such as Ghana, United Kingdom, Germany.
With the use of the Internet, research alternative energy sources and do a presentation in class.
Discuss gender issues related to energy production, supply and usage.
Describe the processes and devices for measuring and metering energy consumption.
In groups, create posters on the advantages of energy conservation to educate others in the community.
Present a report on energy conservation education that you have undertaken.

contentStandards.description: Investigate the natural and human resources around us

indicators.description: Examine the importance of natural resources to the development of Ghana

exemplars.description: Explain what is meant by natural resources.
Through the use of videos or pictures, identify the natural resources of the country, including renewable and non-renewable resources.
On the map of Ghana, show the location of the natural resources.
Discuss efficient ways of exploiting natural resources.
Explain the importance of natural resources for the development of the country.
Discuss the difficulty in exploiting natural resources effectively, including low level of technology, limited technical expertise and limited capital resources.

indicators.description: Evaluate the importance of human resources to the development of Ghana

exemplars.description: Explain what is meant by human resource.
Identify ways of developing human resource.
Through group work, discuss why an educated and trained human resource is the most important asset of the country.
Explain how Ghana’s human resource can be efficiently used in the production of goods and services.
Investigate how some people in the community use their human resource abilities to help the community develop.
Suggest new ways by which they would use their human resource abilities to help develop the community.

contentStandards.description: Evaluate the institution of marriage in Ghana

indicators.description: Examine the importance of marriage as a social institution in Ghana

exemplars.description: Explain the concept of marriage as a social institution.
Discuss ways of contracting marriages in Ghana.
Identify the ways in which marriage is important as a social institution.
Investigate the causes of broken marriages.
Dramatise the effects of broken marriages on the family structure.
Suggest ways of sustaining marriages.

contentStandards.description: Assess the need for responsible parenting in the family

indicators.description: Examine the importance of responsible parenting within the family system

exemplars.description: Explain the concepts: Parenthood and Parenting.
Differentiate parenthood from parenting.
Discuss the responsibilities of parents.
Discuss inappropriate parenting behaviour and its consequences.
Examine how some behaviours by children can cause their parents to act inappropriately.
Suggest ways for handling parent-child conflicts.
Carry out an education programme in the community on the need for parents to be responsible.

contentStandards.description: Analyse the population structure in Ghana and its related issues

indicators.description: Assess population structure in Ghana and its associated development issues

exemplars.description: Recap on Basic 8 work on the population structure in Ghana.
In groups, analyse the effects of rapid population growth on the family, the community and the nation.
Dramatise the effects of large family size on the up keep of the family.
Suggest ways in which social problems and rapid population growth could be minimised.

contentStandards.description: Evaluate the place of culture in national identity

indicators.description: Assess the significance of symbols, music and ceremonies in promoting national identity

exemplars.description: Explain the concept of national identity.
Sing patriotic songs and discuss how songs promote national identity.
With the use of videos or pictures, identify some national and traditional symbols and discuss their features and significance.
Interpret some national and traditional symbols and evaluate their importance in fostering national unity.
Discuss ways of fostering national unity and defending the integrity of the nation.
Discuss how national ceremonies can be used to foster national unity.
Discuss how respecting the customs and culture of other groups plays a part in celebrating diversity in Ghana.

contentStandards.description: Assess the relevance of the 1992 Constitution

indicators.description: Examine the 1992 Constitution and its significance to national development

exemplars.description: Explain the meaning of a constitution.
Outline the main features of the 1992 Constitution.
Use videos or pictures to identify the functions of the three main organs of government.
In groups, discuss the rights, freedoms and obligations of citizens under the 1992 Constitution.
Examine the conditions under which the rights of a citizen can be curtailed by the 1992 Constitution.
Explain the importance of the 1992 Constitution to Ghanaians.

indicators.description: Discuss the rights of the child as enshrined in the 1992 Constitution

exemplars.description: Explain the concepts of child rights.
Examine the provisions of child rights in the 1992 Constitution.
Invite a resource person to discuss the need for children’s rights.
Carry out a project on the responsibilities of children.
Explain the concept of child abuse.
Identify acts that constitute child abuse, including child labour and early marriages.
Examine the effects of child abuse, including physical injury, psychological trauma and poor health.

subStrands.title: PEACE AND SECURITY IN OUR NATION

contentStandards.description: Assess the role of peace and security in national development

indicators.description: Examine the relevance of peace and security in our community

exemplars.description: Explain the concepts of peace and security.
Discuss ways of promoting peace and security.
With the use of video and pictures, compare a country destroyed by conflict and another that has enjoyed a long period of peace.
Using documentaries and pictures, examine safety measures in the community.
Discuss the importance of peace and security in community development.
Role play how peace can be maintained in your neighbourhood.

contentStandards.description: Show understanding of how to promote democracy and political stability

indicators.description: Examine election as a way of promoting democracy and political stability

exemplars.description: Explain the concepts of democracy and election.
Examine the role of free and fair elections in promoting democracy.
Discuss the processes involved in conducting an election.
Identify and discuss the importance of electoral materials.
Watch videos of people casting their votes at a polling station peacefully and discuss your observations.
Demonstrate how free and fair elections can be conducted using role-play.
Assess the role of the Electoral Commission.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the District Assembly concept in Ghana

indicators.description: Examine the role of the District Assembly in promoting decentralisation

exemplars.description: Explain the concept of decentralisation.
Describe the structure of the District Assembly.
Examine the role of District Assemblies in the development of the districts.
Examine the contribution of the Assemblies.
Invite a resource person to talk about the workings of the MMDAs.

contentStandards.description: Evaluate the importance of political stability in Ghana’s development

indicators.description: Assess the significance of political stability in national development

exemplars.description: Explain political stability.
Examine the ways of achieving political stability.
Discuss some of the threats to political stability in the country.
Discuss the importance of political stability.
Suggest ways of promoting political stability in Ghana.

subStrands.title: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
subStrands.description: Role of science and technology in development.

contentStandards.description: Analyse the contribution of science and technology to national development

indicators.description: Examine how science and technology can be used to promote development

exemplars.description: Explain the concepts: Science and Technology.
Examine the difference(s) between ‘Science’ and ‘Technology’.
Discuss how science and technology can be used for development and production in Ghana.
Examine the role of science and technology in specific sectors of the economy.
Investigate and make presentations on the role of science and technology in the development of Ghana.
Examine the problems impeding the development of science and technology in Ghana.
Suggest ways of promoting science and technology in Ghana.
Project: Identify a problem in the school and use the knowledge acquired in science and technology to solve it.

subStrands.title: FINANCIAL AND INVESTMENT ISSUES
subStrands.description: National Pensions Act 766 and PNDC Law 247.

contentStandards.description: Show understanding of the provisions under National Pensions Act 766 and PNDC Law 247

indicators.description: Exhibit knowledge on pension rights under National Pensions Act 766 and PNDC Law 247

exemplars.description: Discuss the provisions under National Pensions Act 766.
In small groups, do a presentation on the provisions under PNDC Law 247.
Invite a resource person to talk about social security in Ghana.
In small groups, do a presentation on the benefits under the Three Tier Pension Scheme.
Research the application processes for the various SSNIT benefits.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding that Ghana had two republics between 1979 and 2000

indicators.description: Explain how the Third Republic came into being (1979-1981)

exemplars.description: Use the internet, print media and oral sources to find out how the Third Republic was established.
Identify the main political parties that took part in the June 1979 elections.
Discuss the outcome of the June 1979 elections.
Dramatise the handing over of power from the AFRC to Dr Hilla Liman’s People’s National Party.

indicators.description: Explain political developments under the Third Republic

exemplars.description: Identify the main features of the 1960 Constitution of the First Republic.
Examine the changes that happened in the country as a result of the 1960 Constitution.
Debate the effects of the changes in the 1960 Republican Constitution.
Describe the membership of the cabinet under the 1960 Constitution.

indicators.description: Explain how the Fourth Republic came into being

exemplars.description: Use the Internet, print media and oral sources to find out how the Fourth Republic was established.
Discuss the outcome of the 28 April 1992 referendum.
Identify the political parties that took part in the 1992 elections.
Discuss the nature of the First Parliament of the Fourth Republic.
Dramatise the inauguration of the first president of the Fourth Republic.
Analyse the 1992 constitution vis-a-vis the American constitution and the Westminster system.

indicators.description: Explain political developments under the Fourth Republic

exemplars.description: Discuss the features of the Fourth Republican constitution.
Debate the pros and cons of the First Parliament of the Fourth Republic.
Assess the advantages of the President being Head of State and Government.
Compare Ghana’s presidential system of government and the Westminster system.
